title: Event Result
description: Sport-generic canonical record for one historical sporting event/result. Successor to result_record.schema.json (Step 2), which is football-only (home_team/away_team/home_score/away_score). This schema generalizes 'two teams with scores' into 'N participants, each with an optional score and/or placement', so the same shape covers team sports, individual sports (tennis, skateboarding), and motorsport without forcing any of them into a football shape. See docs/data-model.md and docs/migration.md.
$comment: Business rule this schema can't express: for exactly two participants with role 'home'/'away' and both numeric scores, 'result' must match the score comparison (see sports_research/validation/business_rules.py: event_result_matches_scores()). No such rule is enforced generically across arbitrary sports/participant shapes — that would require sport-specific knowledge this schema deliberately doesn't encode.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record conforms to.

event_id.description: Stable unique identifier, e.g. '{sport}:{competition-slug}:{season}:{date}:{slug1}-vs-{slug2}' for two-participant events, or '{sport}:{competition-slug}:{season}:{date}:{event-name-slug}' otherwise.

sport.description: Lowercase snake_case sport identifier, e.g. 'football', 'skateboarding', 'tennis', 'motorsport'. Open vocabulary — adding a sport never requires editing this schema.

competition.description: Competition/league/tour/championship name, e.g. 'Premier League', 'Street League Skateboarding', 'Wimbledon', 'Formula 1 World Championship'.

season.description: Canonical season string: 'YYYY' or 'YYYY-YYYY'. Same convention as result_record.schema.json.

event_name.description: Optional specific name for this event beyond competition+season, e.g. 'Men's Singles Final', 'Brazilian Grand Prix', 'Nike SLS Super Crown'. Omit when the competition/season/round already fully identify it (e.g. an ordinary league match).

date.description: ISO 8601 date or date-time of the event.

participants.description: One entry per team/competitor/driver/etc. Two participants with role 'home'/'away' covers football-style events; N participants with 'placement' covers individual/motorsport events.

role.description: Open vocabulary, e.g. 'home', 'away', 'competitor', 'driver', 'team'. Recommended values documented in docs/data-model.md; not schema-enforced, since sports vary.

score.description: Goals/points/sets/time/etc. for this participant, when a single comparable number applies. Null when not applicable/unknown — never invented.

placement.description: Finishing position (1 = first), for placement-based events. Null when not applicable/unknown.

extra.description: Optional freeform sport-specific detail (e.g. {"laps": 71, "time": "1:31:23.199"}). Never required, never validated beyond being an object — this is intentionally the escape hatch for sport-specific detail this schema doesn't try to standardize.

location.description: Optional venue/location details. Renamed from result_record's 'venue' field; same shape.

status.description: Same vocabulary and meaning as result_record.schema.json's 'status'.

result.description: Outcome summary. 'home_win'/'away_win'/'draw' for two-participant home/away events (must match participants' scores — see $comment). 'win' for a single-winner individual/motorsport event where a clear winner exists (identify them via participants[].placement == 1, not by name here). 'unknown' when completed but the outcome couldn't be confirmed. null when not applicable (not completed) or when the event's outcome is fully captured by participants[].placement and no single top-level summary applies (e.g. a multi-heat skateboarding contest).

source_url.description: Direct URL the data was taken from.

verification_status.description: 'unverified': single source, not cross-checked. 'source_confirmed': the specific source itself looks internally consistent/credible but no second independent source has been checked yet. 'verified': cross-checked against at least one independent additional source and consistent. 'conflicting': independent sources disagree, unresolved. 'disputed': the historical record itself is contested independent of this pipeline's sourcing. ('source_confirmed' is new relative to result_record.schema.json's vocabulary — see docs/migration.md.)
